```{=html}
<section class="resources-section">
  <div class="ad-page-container">
    <div class="resource-grid">
      <div class="resource-card">
        <h1 class="section-heading">3D Golf Model Repository</h1>
        <p class="resource-description">
          <a href="https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift" target="_blank" rel="noopener">UpstreamDrift<span class="sr-only">(opens in a new tab)</span></a>
          is a Python simulation and analysis platform for the golf swing. It runs the same model definitions
          through several independent physics engines so that a result can be checked against a second
          implementation rather than taken on trust, and wraps that core in a desktop application, a REST API,
          and a web interface.
        </p>
        <p class="resource-description">
          <strong>Authority snapshot.</strong> The statements on this page describe UpstreamDrift at protected
          <code>main</code> commit
          <a href="https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/tree/98165272f404e6752ec573e05e30a0def7562e0d" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><code>98165272</code><span class="sr-only">(opens in a new tab)</span></a>,
          reviewed 2026-09-02. The upstream repository is the live authority; these are software facts and
          support tiers, not evidence of biomechanical validity or fitness for coaching or clinical use.
        </p>
      </div>

      <div class="resource-card">
        <h2>Overview</h2>
        <p class="resource-description">
          UpstreamDrift covers forward and inverse dynamics, inverse kinematics with nullspace optimization,
          trajectory optimization across candidate swing objectives, kinematic force decomposition (Coriolis,
          centrifugal, gravitational), motion-capture retargeting, and cross-engine comparison that reports the
          deviation between engines. Models range from two-degree-of-freedom pendulums and flexible-shaft
          formulations up to full-body and muscle-driven musculoskeletal models, with parametric humanoid
          generation and URDF export.
        </p>
      </div>

      <div class="resource-card">
        <h2>Physics Engines and Support Tiers</h2>
        <p class="resource-description">
          Support tier states what continuous integration validates, not what is implemented.<br>
          <strong>Supported:</strong> MuJoCo (required on every pull request)<br>
          <strong>Extended:</strong> Drake, Pinocchio (nightly cross-engine validation)<br>
          <strong>Experimental:</strong> OpenSim, MyoSuite (best-effort local validation)<br>
          <strong>Experimental, differentiable:</strong> JaxSim, a JAX-based backend kept in
          <code>src/engines/physics_engines/jaxsim</code> with its own upgrade guard; it has no launcher tile
          and is not part of the published support-tier contract.<br>
          The tier contract is
          <a href="https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/98165272f404e6752ec573e05e30a0def7562e0d/docs/engines/support_tiers.md" target="_blank" rel="noopener">docs/engines/support_tiers.md<span class="sr-only">(opens in a new tab)</span></a>.
        </p>
      </div>

      <div class="resource-card">
        <h2>Architecture</h2>
        <p class="resource-description">
          <strong>Entry point:</strong> <code>python launch_upstream_drift.py</code> starts the local API on port 8000
          and opens the web interface; <code>--classic</code> opens the PyQt6 desktop launcher and
          <code>--api-only</code> runs the server alone.<br>
          <strong>API:</strong> a versioned FastAPI service (<code>src/api</code>) with REST and WebSocket routes.<br>
          <strong>Web UI:</strong> React with Vite, packaged as a Tauri desktop shell (<code>ui/</code>).<br>
          <strong>Rust kernels:</strong> physics kernels in <code>rust_core/</code> (the <code>upstream-physics</code>
          crate, built with maturin) sharing a <code>tools-core</code> crate pinned from the Tools repository.<br>
          <strong>Tooling:</strong> standalone tools under <code>src/tools/</code>, including Pose Studio, the
          Model Explorer, and the launch-monitor analytics workbench.
        </p>
      </div>

      <div class="resource-card">
        <h2>Pipelines and Workbenches</h2>
        <p class="resource-description">
          <strong>Motion pipeline:</strong> video to tracked motion through OpenPose or MediaPipe, with C3D, CSV,
          and JSON import and retargeting onto the simulation models
          (<a href="https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/98165272f404e6752ec573e05e30a0def7562e0d/docs/motion_pipeline/README.md" target="_blank" rel="noopener">motion pipeline guide<span class="sr-only">(opens in a new tab)</span></a>).<br>
          <strong>Launch-monitor analytics:</strong> import, monitor comparison, dispersion, and longitudinal
          trends built on a single canonical model layer shared with the Tools repository
          (<a href="https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/98165272f404e6752ec573e05e30a0def7562e0d/docs/adr/0046-launch-monitor-analytics-single-model-layer.md" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ADR-0046<span class="sr-only">(opens in a new tab)</span></a>).<br>
          <strong>BunkerShot3D:</strong> a designer workbench for sand shots and sole geometry
          (<a href="https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/98165272f404e6752ec573e05e30a0def7562e0d/docs/adr/0032-bunkershot3d-club-design-architecture.md" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ADR-0032<span class="sr-only">(opens in a new tab)</span></a>).<br>
          <strong>Visualization and export:</strong> real-time 3D rendering with force-torque overlays, more than
          ten plot types, and CSV/JSON export.
        </p>
      </div>

      <div class="resource-card">
        <h2>History</h2>
        <p class="resource-description">
          The project began as a MATLAB/Simulink Simscape Multibody model of the golf swing. Those models are
          still in the repository under <code>src/engines/Simscape_Multibody_Models/</code>, maintained as research
          references rather than production artifacts, and are the subject of the
          <a href="../models/models-simulink.html">Simulink Models page</a>. Everything described above is the
          Python platform that grew around them.
        </p>
      </div>

      <div class="resource-card">
        <h2>Requirements and Access</h2>
        <p class="resource-description">
          Windows, macOS, and Linux. Python 3.11 and 3.12 are the tested interpreter minors; Git LFS is required
          because model assets are stored in LFS. MATLAB R2023a or later is needed only for the historical
          MATLAB models.
          <br><br>
          <a href="https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="resource-link">View on GitHub →<span class="sr-only">(opens in a new tab)</span></a>
          <br><br>
          <strong>Clone with Git:</strong><br>
          <code>git clone https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift.git</code>
        </p>
      </div>

      <div class="resource-card">
        <h2>Related Resources</h2>
        <p class="resource-description">
          See the <a href="../pages/overview.html">Overview</a> for the pinned quick start and API example, the
          <a href="../models/programming/index.html">Programming Companion Catalog</a> for the engine, program,
          and workflow inventory, and the <a href="../models/models.html">Golf Modeling Suite</a> for the
          AffineDrift link map.
        </p>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>
```
